title: Can a rollout cap on a sequential certification test be set without losing the 5% error guarantee, and what does it cost?
lede: Follow-up to free-sprtcap: re-tuning a capped SPRT's boundaries and final cut so both errors stay at or below 5% exactly costs, for 1% vs 5% (fixed test 181 rollouts), a mean of 107 rollouts at a cap equal to the fixed size and 90 at twice it, against 90 to 95 for the plain capped test that overshoots the error; the fixed test needs 181.
summary: free-sprtcap showed that simply capping Wald's SPRT inflates the unacceptable-rate error (0.067–0.069 at a cap equal to the fixed test's size). This project re-tunes it: an exact dynamic programme over (trials, failures) searches multiples of Wald's two boundaries (0.5 to 2.5×, each side separately) and every possible final cut for the setting that holds both achieved errors at or below 0.05 and minimises the mean rollouts averaged over the acceptable and unacceptable rates. For p1 = 1% against p0 = 5% (fixed test 181 rollouts) the mean is 107 at a cap of 1× the fixed size, 99 at 1.2–1.3×, 94 at 1.5× and 90 at 2×, always well under 181; the plain capped test is cheaper at small caps (90 to 94) only because it breaks the error guarantee, and at 1.75–2× the re-tuned test is cheaper than it (90.3 against 95.0) while holding the guarantee. Two other (p0, p1) pairs show the same pattern. Rollouts are assumed iid Bernoulli with the twin's failure rate (no sim-to-real gap), the boundary grid is coarse (steps of 0.1×), only the average of the two means is minimised, and nothing is sampled: every number is exact.
